S01.topic: ETL vs ELT Transformation Timing Trade-offs
S01.music: ETL = mastering before mixdown. ELT = recording raw stems then mixing later.

S02.topic: Batch vs Stream Processing Event Time Watermarks Exactly Once Delivery
S02.music: Batch = offline rendering. Stream = live DSP. Watermarks = sync pulse keeping tempo.

S03.topic: Schema Validation Fail Fast vs Degrade Gracefully
S03.music: Schema = key signature. Validation = tuner. Fail fast = hard clip. Degrade = soft limiter.

S04.topic: Data Contracts Ownership SLAs and Governance
S04.music: Data contract = session agreement between producer and engineer. SLA = delivery deadline.

S05.music: Schema evolution = key change mid-song without breaking the groove.

S06.music: Idempotency = playing the same note twice sounds identical. Replay = punch-in recording.

S07.topic: Webhook Ingestion and HMAC Payload Verification
S07.music: Webhook = trigger pad. HMAC = authentication watermark on every hit.

S08.music: Backpressure = sidechain ducking. Buffer = pre-roll before record. Flow control = tempo sync.

S09.music: Vertical = louder amp. Horizontal = more speakers. Both = fill the room differently.

S10.music: Sharding = stem separation. Each shard = isolated track in its own bus.

S11.music: Load balancing = gain staging across channels. Failover = backup vocalist when lead drops.

S12.music: CAP = you can have groove, timing, or loudness — pick two. Partition = dropped connection mid-session.

S13.music: Eventual consistency = all musicians arrive at the same chord. Consensus = the conductor.

S14.music: Checksum = audio fingerprint. Hash = unique waveform ID. Fingerprint = Shazam signature.

S15.music: ACID = studio-perfect take. BASE = live performance with acceptable drift.

S16.music: WAL = pre-roll tape before record. Durable queue = tape that survives power loss.

S17.music: Merkle tree = stem hierarchy. Content-addressed = every sample named by its own waveform hash.

S18.music: Lineage = session history log. Provenance = who played what on which take.

S19.topic: Retries Dead Letter Queues and Error Isolation
S19.music: Dead letter queue = outtakes folder. Retry = punch-in attempt. Isolation = mute the bad track.

S20.topic: Circuit Breakers Exponential Backoff and FinOps
S20.music: Circuit breaker = overload protection on the amp. Backoff = cooling down between takes. FinOps = studio budget.

S21.music: Checkpoint = save state mid-session. Replay = reconstruct the exact performance from MIDI data.

S22.music: Distributed trace = following a single note across every instrument in the arrangement.

S23.music: Zero trust = every musician re-verifies identity each session. Secret rotation = changing studio access codes.

S24.music: Memory masking = noise gate on sensitive frequencies. Anonymization = stripping metadata from exported stems.

S25.topic: Memory JSON Atomic Writes Multi-Agent Consensus and Self-Healing Pipelines
S25.music: Atomic write = punch-in that either lands perfect or not at all. Consensus = all agents agree on the one true memory. Self-healing = the track fixes itself when a stem goes missing.
